McLaren: McLaren has tweaked the rear wing by reshaping the endplates to smooth the airflow and by fitting a brand‑new wing assembly that cuts drag on this circuit. The result is a cleaner rear‑end aerodynamic balance, giving the car more straight‑line speed without sacrificing stability. In short, the changes should help the team hit higher top speeds and stay glued to the track through the fast corners this weekend.
Mercedes F1 Team: Mercedes has tweaked the rear wing to a lower‑drag setting for this circuit, flattening the upper elements so the car can pull a bit more straight‑line speed down the long laps. The small rear‑corner “drum” winglets have been repositioned and lengthened to give the car more stable down‑force when it’s on the edge of grip, while the front‑wing endplates now sit with a higher angle to smooth the airflow into the car’s nose. Together, these changes should help the team keep the car fast on the straights without sacrificing the bite needed in the twisty sections of the weekend’s track.
Red Bull Racing: Red Bull’s rear wing now features reshaped pylons – essentially the little “spines” that help the wing work. The new shape gives the aero a cleaner, more consistent bite on the straights and corners, letting the car stay glued to the track while still delivering strong straight‑line speed. In practice, that translates to better stability and more tyre life over the weekend, giving the team a solid edge in qualifying and the race.
Scuderia Ferrari: Scuderia Ferrari did not submit any updates for this event.
Williams Racing: Williams has tweaked three key aero pieces for this weekend: a new rear‑brake duct winglet to clean up airflow and shave off drag, a local trim on the floor’s main body to smooth the car’s ride on this particular circuit, and a reshaped floor diffuser that creates a bigger “sweet‑spot” under the car for extra rear‑end grip. Together these changes should make the car both faster on the straights and more stable through the fast corners, giving the team a better chance to fight higher up the grid.
Racing Bulls / RB: Racing Bulls have reshaped the car’s aerodynamics this weekend, tweaking the side‑pods, upper bodywork and even the roll‑hoop inlet to smooth airflow and give the car a steadier, higher‑down‑force feel on the straights and through corners. The updated brake‑drum assembly at the front and a new upper rear‑wing element tighten the car’s balance, helping drivers keep the tires in their sweet spot longer. In short, the package should boost corner‑entry grip and stability, giving the team a better chance to fight for points on the upcoming track.
Aston Martin: Aston Martin did not submit any updates for this event.
Haas F1 Team: Haas has tweaked the front wing to give the car a bit more bite on the straights and a smoother feel in the corners—think a cleaner, more stable front end that sticks to the track. The new wing shape also trims a little drag, so the car can accelerate faster out of the slow turns that dominate this weekend’s circuit. In short, the updates should help Haas hit higher speeds on the straights while staying more planted through the twists.
Audi F1 Team: Audi has tweaked the upper part of the rear wing to suit this circuit’s layout, fine‑tuning the amount of drag so the car can stay quicker on the straights without losing grip in the corners. They’ve also added a small winglet on the diffuser’s sidewall, which cleans up the airflow at the back of the car and gives a bit more rear stability. Together, these changes should translate into better corner exit speed and more confidence when pushing on the high‑speed sections of the weekend’s track.
Alpine F1 Team: Alpine has reshaped the halo fairing and added a small winglet, smoothing airflow over the car’s cockpit area. The tweak reduces drag and gives a bit more down‑force to the front end, helping the car grip better through the high‑speed corners this weekend. In short, it’s a subtle aerodynamic boost that could translate into a few tenths of a second on the lap.
Cadillac: Cadillac has tweaked the front‑wing endplates – reshaping the footplate, adding new turning vanes and a horizontal vane on the body – to smooth the air that hits the car’s front. The result is a cleaner “air tunnel” that boosts downforce and gives the tires more grip, so the car will feel steadier through corners and can push harder on the straights this weekend. In short, the update should translate into better handling and a quicker lap time without the team having to change any driving style.
